title: The Fred Allen Show
paragraphs: Long-running topical comedy-variety vehicle for Fred Allen and Portland Hoffa under multiple historical titles.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Linit Bath Club Revue (October 23, 1932 to April 16, 1933), Salad Bowl Revue (August 4, 1933 to December 1, 1933), Sal Hepatica / Hour of Smiles transition (January 3, 1934 to July 4, 1934), and Town Hall Tonight (July 11, 1934 to September 27, 1939).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Fred Allen (performer and writer), Portland Hoffa (performer), Minerva Pious (performer), Al Goodman and His Orchestra (performer), Kenny Delmar (performer and announcer), The De Marco Sisters (performer), and Parker Fennelly (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].

The stories often return to radio industry and broadcasting satire, music and performance, advertising, shopping and consumer culture, wartime and military life, topical news and current-events satire, and Hollywood and celebrity culture.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Topical satire in network radio comedy, American network comedy during World War II, and Postwar network comedy and emerging television competition.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-big-show|The Big Show]], [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], and [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]].
